patients.summary: Undergraduate who joins at 20 with recurrent HSV-1 cold sores, develops type 1 diabetes in 2021 managed by endocrinology, and has recurrent stress-related jaundice attributed by GI to both Dubin-Johnson and Gilbert syndromes. Laparoscopic appendectomy in 2023; heat exhaustion ED visit in July 2026 after his last practice visit.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called asking to become a patient. 20 y/o, starting his second year at college, living in Williamsburg. Previously seen at a family practice near his parents' home. Student health insurance plan, card info taken. Only med is valacyclovir as needed for cold sores. New pt visit booked 9/10 at 9:00. Release signed by pt over the portal; request for records sent to the prior office.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

20 y/o man here to set up primary care now that he is at school locally year-round. Feels well. No concerns today beyond keeping his valacyclovir on file.

PMH: cold sores (HSV-1) since about age 15. Gets 2-4 a year, usually around exams or when run down. Takes valacyclovir 500 mg twice a day when he feels the tingle, stops once crusted. No eye involvement ever.
PSH: none.
Meds: valacyclovir 500 mg BID prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father has type 2 diabetes. Mother has hypothyroidism (autoimmune). Older brother was told he has Gilbert syndrome. A cousin on his dad's side has Dubin-Johnson syndrome. Pt has never had his own liver tests that he knows of and has never been yellow.
Social: undergraduate, lives with a roommate off campus. Never smoked, no alcohol, no drugs. Plays pickup soccer most weekends. Single.

ROS: negative in full.

Exam: vitals as charted. Thin, well. HEENT normal, no active lip lesions. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin clear. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. Recurrent herpes labialis - continue episodic valacyclovir, refills given.
2. Health maintenance - prior records requested to confirm childhood series; flu shot at a nurse visit next month. Labs at a physical next year.
PHQ-2 0.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Records from prior family practice
documents.author: outside family medicine
documents.body:
Summary of care, outside family medicine office, patient seen from infancy through 2019.

Problems: herpes labialis, recurrent.
Medications: valacyclovir 500 mg tablets, one twice daily as needed at onset of lesions.
Allergies: none known.
Immunizations: hepatitis B series complete in infancy; MMR x2; varicella x2; DTaP series and IPV complete; Tdap at age 12; HPV series complete; meningococcal conjugate x2 (last at 16).
Well visits yearly through adolescence with normal growth and development. Sports physicals on file.

Scanned to chart.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PHYSICAL

Classes mostly remote this fall, still in his apartment in town. Doing fine. Two cold sores since spring, both settled within a few days on valacyclovir. Sleeping ok, some late nights. Soccer has been on hold.

Meds: valacyclovir prn. NKDA.
FH/SH unchanged: never smoker, no alcohol.

ROS negative.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well, thin. Lips without lesions. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Skin clear, no jaundice. Normal gait.

PHQ-9: 2.

A/P
- Health maintenance: one-time HIV and hepatitis C screens today along with BMP, CBC and lipids. Flu shot given today.
- Recurrent HSV-1 labialis: stable, refills current.
Follow up in a year.

documents.title: Your physical labs

documents.title: Thirst and weight loss
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called back after his message this morning. About a month of being thirsty all the time, carrying a water bottle everywhere, up several times a night to pee, and he thinks he has lost weight even though he is eating more than usual. Some blurry vision this past week. Tired. No vomiting, no belly pain, no trouble breathing. Father has diabetes.

This story in a 22 y/o is new diabetes until proven otherwise. Our endocrinology colleagues had an urgent new-patient opening Thursday morning and he will take it; they will draw his labs there. Told him that if he starts vomiting, can't keep fluids down, gets belly pain or fast/deep breathing, or feels confused, he goes to the ED that day and does not wait for Thursday. He repeated this back. Will call him Friday.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 05/27/2021
Referred by: primary care physician
Reason: thirst, urinary frequency and weight loss

Thank you for sending this 22-year-old student. For roughly four weeks he has felt worn out and constantly thirsty; by his estimate he is getting through close to five liters of water a day, and he now gets up more than once a night to void. He is hungrier than usual and still down about 6 kg over the month. In the last week he has had intermittent blurring when reading or working on his laptop. No dysuria or urgency, no abdominal pain. No fever, rash or joint pains.

History: recurrent cold sores on as-needed valacyclovir. No surgery. No known drug allergies. Father with type 2 diabetes, mother with autoimmune hypothyroidism; an older brother and a paternal cousin with inherited bilirubin conditions. No tobacco, alcohol or drugs.

Exam: BP 106/64, pulse 92, afebrile. Weight 64 kg. Thin young man who looks a little dry, mucous membranes dry. Acuity mildly reduced and briefly sharper after blinking; fundi normal on direct ophthalmoscopy. Genitourinary and neurologic examinations normal.

Impression: symptomatic hyperglycemia in a lean young adult, most likely new autoimmune diabetes. Not acidotic on history or exam.

Plan: same-day labs - BMP, A1c, urinalysis, GAD65 antibody, C-peptide, TSH and tTG-IgA. He will return tomorrow to go over results and start treatment. ED precautions reviewed.

Results addendum 05/28: glucose 388 mg/dL, bicarbonate 23, A1c 11.6%, urine glucose 3+ with moderate ketones, GAD65 antibody positive at 34 IU/mL, C-peptide 0.4 ng/mL. TSH and tTG-IgA normal.

Allergies: NKDA.
Endocrinology

medications.drug: 3 ML insulin glargine 100 UNT/ML Pen Injector
medications.sig: Inject 16 units under the skin at bedtime

medications.drug: 3 ML insulin lispro 100 UNT/ML Pen Injector
medications.sig: Inject under the skin with meals per sliding scale

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up: insulin start
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 05/28/2021

Seen back the morning after his consultation to review labs. Glucose 388, A1c 11.6%, GAD65 antibody positive, low C-peptide, moderate ketonuria with a normal bicarbonate. Thyroid and celiac screens normal.

Diagnosis: type 1 diabetes mellitus, new. No DKA.

Treatment started today:
- insulin glargine 16 units subcutaneously at bedtime
- insulin lispro with meals on a sliding scale (scale given in writing)
Meter, strips and pen needles prescribed. Pen technique taught and he gave his first dose in clinic. Hypoglycemia recognition and treatment reviewed. Diabetes educator session and nutrition visit next week. He will send readings through our portal for titration, return in about 6 to 8 weeks.

Allergies: NKDA.
Endocrinology

[received by fax 06/22/2021]

documents.title: Check-in after endocrinology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called as promised. He saw endocrinology yesterday and again today and they told him it is type 1 diabetes. He is on two insulin pens and did his first shot in their office. Feels a bit overwhelmed but has the plan in writing and an educator visit next week. Video visit with me in about 10 days to go over everything.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at his apartment, identity confirmed, consents to video.

Ten days into insulin for new type 1 diabetes (endocrinology dx 5/28 - their letter not in yet, history from pt and his written plan). Glargine 16 units at bedtime, lispro with meals per their scale. Fasting readings coming down, mostly 130s-170s now, one reading in the 70s before dinner that he treated with juice. Thirst and night urination are gone. Vision back to normal. Saw the educator Friday.

Mood: understandably thrown by this but has good support, roommate knows how to help with a low. Mom has been helpful.

A/P
1. Type 1 diabetes, new - endocrinology managing insulin. Updated our med list from his pens. Will request their notes.
2. Recurrent cold sores - valacyclovir prn unchanged.
Call with anything; next in person in the fall.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 08/17/2021

Type 1 diabetes, about 12 weeks on basal-bolus insulin. Doing well. Has regained most of the lost weight. Logs show fasting values mostly in range, a few post-dinner highs on late nights, two mild lows after soccer that he treated himself. A1c drawn today, now improved from 11.6% at diagnosis.

Regimen unchanged: glargine 16 units at bedtime, lispro sliding scale with meals. Reviewed carrying fast sugar during sports. Next visit in 3 months.

Endocrinology

events.reason: Diabetes check-in; episodes of yellow eyes

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: recurrent episodes of scleral icterus; family history of inherited bilirubin disorders

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: First in-person visit since his diabetes diagnosis. Endocrinology following, saw them in August; he says his A1c was much better. Glargine 16 at bedtime, lispro by scale. Two or three mild lows, all around soccer, none needing help.

New item he wanted to bring up: a few times over the last year, when he has been sick or under a lot of stress, his eyes have gone yellow for a few days and then cleared. He has not had it checked. No itching, no belly pain, urine and stool normal colors each time. Not yellow now. Brother has Gilbert's and a cousin on dad's side has Dubin-Johnson, so he wonders.

O: vitals as charted. No scleral icterus today, skin normal color. Abdomen soft, nontender, no liver or spleen felt. Lips clear. Feet: skin intact, normal sensation.

A/P
1. Recurrent episodes of scleral icterus with a family history of two inherited bilirubin disorders - referral to GI; asked him to let GI know if it happens again before the appointment so they can catch labs during a spell.
2. Type 1 diabetes - per endocrinology. Lipids and urine microalbumin today.
3. Cold sores - quiet.
Flu shot done last month.

documents.title: Cholesterol and urine results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cholesterol numbers are normal and there is no protein leaking into the urine, which is what we watch for with diabetes. GI referral is in; their office should call you to schedule.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 11/30/2021
Reason for referral: recurrent jaundice

He happens to be in the middle of an episode today: two days of mild yellowing of the skin and eyes. Over the past year he has had a handful of similar spells, generally when he was ill or stressed, each clearing by itself. Type 1 diabetes was diagnosed about six months ago and is managed by endocrinology. He has no itch, abdominal pain, dark urine or pale stools.

Meds: insulin glargine 16 units at bedtime, insulin lispro sliding scale, valacyclovir prn. NKDA.
Family: older brother with Gilbert syndrome; paternal cousin with Dubin-Johnson syndrome. He adds that his mother has had spells of yellow eyes herself that were never worked up. Father with type 2 diabetes, mother with autoimmune hypothyroidism.
Social: student, no tobacco, alcohol or drugs.

Exam: scleral icterus. Liver edge palpable and slightly tender at the costal margin. Otherwise normal, no stigmata of chronic liver disease.

Labs today: total bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL, direct 2.5, indirect 0.7. ALT 45, AST 40, alkaline phosphatase 90 U/L.

Assessment: predominantly conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal transaminases and alkaline phosphatase, in a young man with a family member carrying the same diagnosis. Most consistent with Dubin-Johnson syndrome, a benign inherited disorder of bilirubin excretion.

Plan: right upper quadrant ultrasound to make sure there is no obstruction. No treatment needed. Reviewed that spells may come with illness, fasting or stress. Return in about 6 months or sooner with a prolonged episode.

Gastroenterology

reports.text:
Indication: conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, evaluate for obstruction.
Technique: grayscale and color Doppler imaging of the right upper quadrant.
Findings: The liver is normal in size and echotexture with smooth contour; no focal lesion. Hepatopetal portal venous flow. The gallbladder is normally distended without stones, sludge or wall thickening; sonographic Murphy sign negative. Common bile duct measures 3 mm. No intrahepatic ductal dilation. Visualized pancreas unremarkable. Right kidney normal. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Normal right upper quadrant ultrasound. No biliary dilation or gallstones.

documents.title: Ultrasound reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: RUQ ultrasound ordered by GI, copy to us: normal liver, gallbladder and ducts. Fits the GI impression of Dubin-Johnson. Problem list updated from the GI letter. Nothing further from our side.

documents.title: Dubin-Johnson question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The GI doctor said I have Dubin-Johnson like my cousin. Is it something I need to tell people about, like if I go to the ER for my diabetes? And does it mess with insulin at all?

documents.title: Re: Dubin-Johnson question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good questions. It does not affect your insulin or your diabetes. It is worth mentioning to any new doctor or ER, because your bilirubin can run high and it saves people from chasing it. Your ultrasound was normal too. It's on your problem list here so anyone looking at your chart will see it.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 02/08/2022

Type 1 diabetes, 8 months out. Meter download reviewed: good overnight stability, post-meal spikes when he guesses carbs at the dining hall. Occasional mild lows with exercise, self-treated. A1c drawn today.
Also has new GI diagnosis of Dubin-Johnson syndrome, no bearing on diabetes management.

Plan: no dose change. Glargine 16 units at bedtime, lispro sliding scale. Carb counting refresher with our dietitian. Return 4 months.

Allergies: NKDA.
Endocrinology

documents.title: Prior authorization: insulin glargine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: new plan year on the student policy requires PA for glargine pens. Form completed with diagnosis type 1 diabetes, on basal insulin since 5/2021. Submitted online, approved same day for 12 months. Pharmacy and pt notified.

documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 05/24/2022

Seen back with another spell: two days of yellow eyes and skin, right in the middle of final exams, sleeping little and eating at odd hours. No pain, itch, or change in urine or stool color.

Exam: looks well; scleral icterus. Abdomen soft and nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly.

Labs: total bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL with direct 0.4 and indirect 2.8. AST 30, ALT 28, alkaline phosphatase 70 U/L. CBC normal.

Assessment: this episode is unconjugated, with a normal blood count and normal liver enzymes, after fasting and poor sleep - the typical picture of Gilbert syndrome, which his brother has. This is in addition to the Dubin-Johnson syndrome diagnosed in November on a conjugated pattern. Both are benign.

Plan: regular meals and sleep around exams; no treatment. Follow up as needed.

Gastroenterology

[Received 10/04/2022 in response to records request]

documents.title: No-show follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not come to 2:20 appt. Left voicemail. Pt called back at 4, working a summer job and forgot. Rebooked as his physical on 9/20.

documents.title: Rooming
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Roomed for physical. Meds reviewed with pt: glargine 16 u qhs, lispro per scale, valacyclovir prn. NKDA. Fingerstick at home this morning 126. PHQ-9 completed: 3. Wants flu and covid today; ok with other vaccines if due.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PHYSICAL

Back for senior year (taking the slow route, working part-time). Diabetes is steady with endocrinology every few months. Lows only with long soccer games, he carries glucose tabs.

He tells me GI saw him in May during another yellow spell at finals and told him he 'also has Gilbert's.' We never got that note. Front desk will request it.

Cold sores: one in the spring, valacyclovir worked.

Meds as rooming note. NKDA.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI about 22. Well. No icterus today. Mouth and lips clear. Neck without thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Feet: no calluses or skin breaks, monofilament and vibration intact, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. Type 1 diabetes - A1c, microalbumin with labs today; CMP, CBC, lipids, TSH (mother's thyroid disease, his own autoimmune diabetes). Eye exam - due, has an optometrist in town, will book.
2. Dubin-Johnson and reported Gilbert syndrome - records request to GI.
3. Immunizations: flu, bivalent covid booster, Tdap (last at 12), and PCV20 given his diabetes.
4. PHQ-9 3.
RTC 1 year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: GI records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to the outside GI office for notes and labs from pt's May 2022 visit. Will follow up in two weeks if nothing arrives.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your A1c is right where endocrinology has been getting it, kidneys and urine protein are normal, and cholesterol and thyroid are normal. Bilirubin is a bit over the lab's upper limit with normal liver enzymes, which is what we expect with your bilirubin conditions - no action. Please do book that eye exam.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Diabetic eye exam letter, outside optometry practice. Exam date 11/03/2022.
Best corrected acuity 20/20 OD and OS. Pupils normal. Pressures normal. Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy either eye, no macular edema.
Recommend repeat dilated exam in 12 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Same-day slot. Two days of yellow eyes and a yellowish tinge to his skin. He has been studying for exams and skipping meals, not much sleep. Feels fine otherwise. No pain, no itching, urine and stool look normal. Sugars a little higher than usual with the odd eating, no lows. Same pattern as the spells GI has seen (Dubin-Johnson in 2021, then a Gilbert-type spell last May).

Meds: glargine 16 u qhs, lispro scale, valacyclovir prn. NKDA.

O: vitals as charted. Looks well. Scleral icterus. Abdomen soft, nontender, liver and spleen not enlarged.

A/P
Recurrent jaundice in known Gilbert and Dubin-Johnson syndromes, triggered by fasting and short sleep. Hepatic panel with fractionation and CBC today to make sure it looks like his usual. Regular meals even during exams - set alarms if needed, which also helps the diabetes. Expect it to clear in a few days; call if it lingers past 2 weeks or if he gets pain, dark urine or pale stool.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Bilirubin is 3.2, mostly the indirect kind, with normal liver enzymes and a normal blood count. Same picture GI saw last spring. Nothing to treat. Eat regularly and it should fade over the next several days.

documents.title: Re: Liver tests
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. Already looking less yellow today. Back to actual meals.

documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 03/07/2023

Type 1 diabetes since 05/2021. Steady control. Meter average stable, highest readings in late January during exams with irregular meals. No severe hypoglycemia. A1c today.

Glargine 16 units at bedtime and lispro sliding scale continued. Discussed exercise snacks for the spring soccer season. Return 4 to 6 months.

Endocrinology

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Indication: right lower quadrant pain.
Technique: axial CT of the abdomen and pelvis after intravenous contrast, with coronal and sagittal reformats.
Findings: The appendix is dilated with wall enhancement and surrounding fat stranding. No appendicolith. No extraluminal gas, fluid collection or abscess. Liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys are normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. Lung bases clear. No acute osseous abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Acute uncomplicated appendicitis. No perforation or abscess.

documents.title: Operative report: laparoscopic appendectomy
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 07/13/2023
Preoperative diagnosis: acute appendicitis
Postoperative diagnosis: same, uncomplicated
Procedure: laparoscopic appendectomy
Anesthesia: general endotracheal
Findings: inflamed, nonperforated appendix; no abscess or purulent fluid.
Description: three-port technique with umbilical access. Mesoappendix divided with energy device, base secured with a stapler. Specimen retrieved in a bag. Ports closed, skin with absorbable suture and glue.
EBL minimal. No complications. Insulin managed per perioperative protocol with endocrinology input by phone.
Pathology: acute appendicitis.
Allergies: NKDA.

[Scanned 09/05/2023]

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 07/13/2023 via the emergency department
Discharged: 07/14/2023

24-year-old man with type 1 diabetes, Gilbert and Dubin-Johnson syndromes, who came in overnight with right lower quadrant pain. WBC 13.4. CT showed uncomplicated acute appendicitis. Taken for laparoscopic appendectomy the same morning without complication. Pathology: acute appendicitis.

Hospital course: tolerated diet by the evening of surgery, pain controlled on acetaminophen, walking. Glucose managed on his home basal insulin with correction lispro. Discharged postoperative day 1.

Discharge medications: home insulin glargine 16 units at bedtime and lispro sliding scale; valacyclovir as needed; acetaminophen 500 mg 1 to 2 tablets every 6 hours as needed.
Activity: no heavy lifting or contact sports for 2 weeks.
Follow-up: general surgery clinic in 1 week.
Allergies: NKDA.

[Received 09/05/2023 after second request]

documents.title: Had my appendix out
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just letting you know I had my appendix out last Thursday at the hospital. Went in at night with bad pain on the right side, they did a CT and took it out laparoscopically that morning. Home since Friday, feeling ok, only taking Tylenol. I see the surgeon this week.

documents.title: Re: Had my appendix out
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry you went through that, and glad it went smoothly. Keep an eye on your sugars while you're less active and eating less. We'll ask the hospital for the records. Let's do a short video check after you've seen the surgeon.

documents.title: General surgery postoperative visit
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GENERAL SURGERY CLINIC - POSTOPERATIVE VISIT
Date of visit: 07/21/2023

One week out from laparoscopic appendectomy for uncomplicated acute appendicitis. Recovering well. For the last two days the whites of his eyes have looked yellow to him. No abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; bowels normal; passing gas; eating well, appetite better than in the hospital. No fevers or chills, no dark urine or pale stools. Walks every day. A little tired. Using acetaminophen now and then.
Known Gilbert and Dubin-Johnson syndromes with previous yellow spells during exam periods in 2022 and early 2023. He mentions his father was once told of 'some liver enzyme issue' that was never treated.

Exam: afebrile. Scleral icterus, skin not jaundiced. Abdomen soft, nontender. Port sites healed, no erythema, no fluid collection.

Labs: total bilirubin 3.1 mg/dL, indirect 2.8, direct 0.3. AST, ALT and alkaline phosphatase normal. Hemoglobin and hematocrit normal.

Impression: normal recovery. Icterus is an unconjugated rise consistent with his Gilbert syndrome after surgery and reduced intake, not a surgical complication.
Plan: resume full activity including soccer after 2 weeks from surgery. No further surgical follow-up needed.

Allergies: NKDA.
General Surgery

Video visit, pt at home, identity confirmed.

Follow-up after laparoscopic appendectomy 7/13 at the regional hospital. Incisions look healed on camera.

Physical next year; flu in the fall.

documents.author: optometry

Diabetic eye exam report, outside optometry practice. Exam date 11/09/2023.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 01/23/2024

Type 1 diabetes, 2.5 years. Appendectomy last July went smoothly. Busy term with a part-time job, more skipped lunches and evening highs. No severe lows. A1c today, a little above last year's.

OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY NOTE
Date of visit: 05/22/2024

25-year-old man with recurrent HSV-1, type 1 diabetes and Gilbert syndrome that flares with stress. Three days of painful sores on the lips and inside the mouth, with a mild fever. A tingling feeling in the area came first, then the blisters. He has had this a number of times, mostly with stress or short sleep.

Meds: insulin glargine, insulin lispro, valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily as needed. NKDA.

Exam: grouped vesicles and shallow erosions limited to the perioral skin and the oral mucosa. No eye involvement. No lesions elsewhere.

Assessment: herpes simplex virus infection, recurrence of his known HSV-1, clinical diagnosis.
Plan: take his valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily as prescribed now; supportive care with fluids and soft foods. Return or call for any eye pain or redness, or if lesions spread.

Dermatology

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 26 y/o with Gilbert and Dubin-Johnson syndromes and T1DM. His roommate told him this morning his eyes were yellow. Got back last night from five days camping, where food was limited and meals were irregular - ate very little some days. A bit tired since getting home, which he puts down to not drinking enough and poor sleep in the tent. No belly pain, nausea, vomiting, weight loss, itch or dark urine. No recent illness, no alcohol or drugs, no new meds or supplements. Sugars ran a little high on the trip, no lows. Spells before this: exam periods in 2022 and early 2023 and after his appendectomy in July 2023. He also remembers one earlier in college after a few all-nighters and skipped meals that went away on its own.

Meds: glargine 16 u qhs, lispro scale, valacyclovir prn. NKDA. PSH: lap appendectomy 2023.
FH: older brother with Gilbert syndrome, paternal cousin with Dubin-Johnson.

O: vitals normal, BMI 22. Well, no distress, alert and oriented. Scleral icterus; skin not jaundiced. No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly, liver span normal to percussion. No spider angiomas, palmar erythema or ascites. Heart and lungs normal. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
Icteric spell after several days of poor intake, in known Gilbert syndrome (with Dubin-Johnson). Hepatic panel with fractionation and CBC to confirm the usual unconjugated pattern. Fluids, regular meals, sleep. No further workup unless the labs look different from his past spells.

documents.title: Bilirubin results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Bilirubin 2.6, almost all indirect; liver enzymes normal; hemoglobin 14, normal. Same Gilbert-type spell you've had before after not eating much. No treatment needed. Pack more food next trip!

events.reason: Lightheadedness and nausea after soccer in the heat

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of visit: 07/11/2026

CC: lightheaded, dizzy and nauseated after soccer.

HPI: 27-year-old man with type 1 diabetes, Gilbert syndrome and Dubin-Johnson syndrome (most recent jaundice spell May 2025). Played about three hours at a summer soccer tournament in direct sun with no real breaks. Drank water through the day but ate little. Over the last hour felt lightheaded, dizzy and queasy and teammates brought him in.

Meds: insulin glargine 16 units at bedtime, insulin lispro sliding scale, valacyclovir prn. PSH: laparoscopic appendectomy. NKDA. No tobacco, alcohol or drugs.

Triage vitals: T 39.5 C (103.1 F), HR 110, BP 100/60, RR 22, SpO2 98% on room air.
Exam: skin cool and moist. Fatigued, oriented x3. Remainder of exam unremarkable.

Labs: Na 135, K 4.2, Cl 100, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.0, glucose 90.

ED course: moved to a cool room, ice packs and fans. Normal saline 2 L IV. Glucose rechecked by fingerstick and stayed in range with oral intake. Repeat vitals T 37.6 C, HR 86, BP 114/70. Nausea and dizziness gone, walking without symptoms, tolerating fluids.

Diagnoses: heat exhaustion; dehydration.
Disposition: discharged home with a friend. Rest and fluids for 24-48 hours, no sports until fully recovered, check glucose more often for the next day. Follow up with primary care as needed.

[Received 08/11/2026, filed]

documents.title: Went to the ER Saturday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted to tell you I ended up in the ER Saturday after a soccer tournament - got dizzy and sick to my stomach in the heat. They said heat exhaustion and dehydration, gave me two bags of fluid and sent me home. Feeling normal now. Sugars were fine the whole time.

documents.title: Re: Went to the ER Saturday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you're feeling back to normal. Take it easy for a few more days, build back slowly, and on hot days take real breaks in the shade with fluids and some salt and carbs, checking your sugar before and after. If dizziness or nausea come back, call us. We'll get the ER record for your chart.
